analysis.answer:
No non-learning controller beats v3w on delay and close-following together in any cell or level (0 of 9). None beats it on delay alone either: 0 of 58 v3w-against-rule delay CIs lie below 0 (44 favour v3w, 14 are ties). On close-following alone, only no control beats it: in X1 (−16.6 [−25.1, −8.4]), at B 3,500 (−272.7 [−303.6, −87.3], which is 21.9 against 5.5 veh·s per run) and at B 7,000 (−70.4 [−76.1, −62.1]).

- **X1 at 5,300 veh/h:** v3w is ahead of all 14 rules on delay (+5.0 to +11.6 %), on close-following (+18.8 to +44.7 %) and on flow.
- **X2 at 5,300 veh/h:** v3w is ahead of 13 of 14 rules on delay. It ties os0_10_10 (+2.4 [−0.6, +7.5]) and is narrowly ahead of 3E-X2 (+3.0 [+0.7, +5.6]) and lr1000_10_1 (+4.1 [+0.2, +5.4]). It is ahead of all 14 rules on close-following (smallest margins: 3E-T +11.5 [+5.6, +16.2], 3E-X2 +12.3 [+5.0, +18.7]) and ties no control there (−0.9 [−5.8, +9.5]).
- **Band (4,500–6,000) and S1 (3,500, 7,000):** only no control, p333, os1_15_10 and 3E-T were run.
  - v3w ties p333 and os1_15_10 on delay at every level from 3,500 to 6,000. It is ahead of both at 7,000 (+3.7 [+2.6, +5.2] and +6.6 [+1.6, +9.9]).
  - It ties them on close-following from 3,500 to 5,250, and is ahead of both at 5,500, 6,000 and 7,000 (+24.7 to +46.5 %).
  - It is ahead of 3E-T on delay from 3,500 to 6,000 (at 4,500 only marginally) and ties 3E-T at 7,000 on both delay and close-following.
- **Braking is where rules are ahead.** On b45 (seconds at −4.5 m/s² or harder), 3E-T is ahead in X1 (−16.1 [−21.3, −10.2]), X2 (−8.5), at 6,000 (−9.8) and at 7,000 (−29.7). copy is ahead in X1 (−5.4). On b3, 3E-T is ahead at 3,500 (−2.2) and no control in several cells.
- **Delay/close-following front (point estimates):** v3w lies beyond the rule front in X1, X2, and at 5,250, 5,500, 6,000 and 7,000. At 4,500 and 5,000 its position depends on the point method. At 3,500 it is inside the front: p333 (= os1_15_10, identical runs) is better by 390 veh·s of delay and 0.4 veh·s of close-following, both CIs ties.
- **tail and sw** show the same pattern: no rule is ahead on delay anywhere, and only no control is ahead on close-following.
- **Count:** 790 unadjusted 95 % CIs.

findings.statement: X1 at 5,300 veh/h: v3w is ahead of every one of the 14 rules on delay, close-following and flow. Only no control is ahead of v3w, on close-following and braking. On b45, 3E-T and copy are also ahead.
findings.method: common1.raw (conf3/common.py) at pct (2.5, 97.5): paired seeds; arm = arm_mean over w0u250, w1u500, w2u250, w3u500, w4u500 (confirmed by decide2.names on validation.json); sign −1 for delay/ttc_net/b3/b45 and +1 for passed; 20,000 resamples, rng 20261104; 40 seeds 7,440,840-879.
findings.evidence: tables.md sections '### X1: v3w against each controller' and 'X1: which rules beat...'; results.json cells['X1|5300'].

findings.statement: X2 at 5,300 veh/h: no rule is ahead of v3w on delay or close-following. v3w ties os0_10_10 on delay and flow, and ties no control on close-following. 3E-T is ahead on b45, and no control on b3.
findings.evidence: tables.md '### X2: v3w against each controller'; results.json cells['X2|5300'].

findings.statement: Band B (4,500-6,000 veh/h, 20 seeds; only no control, p333, os1_15_10 and 3E-T were run): no rule is ahead of v3w on delay or close-following at any level. On delay, v3w ties p333 and os1_15_10 at all five levels and is ahead of 3E-T and no control. On close-following, v3w ties p333 and os1_15_10 at 4,500-5,250 and is ahead of them at 5,500 and 6,000.
findings.method: As F1; cell B, seeds 7,440,880-899, 20 per level; 4 opponents per level.
findings.evidence: tables.md section (2), '### B at 4,500 ... 6,000 veh/h'. The v3w-against-no-control band values equal round 2's stored test_result.json['band']['v3w'] to every digit (for example 4,500 close-following −121.62 [−155.14, +7.30]).

findings.statement: S1 (cell B at 3,500 and 7,000 veh/h, 20 seeds, v3w only). At 3,500: p333 and os1_15_10 are the same runs; v3w ties them on delay and close-following, is ahead of 3E-T on delay, and 3E-T is ahead on b3. At 7,000: v3w is ahead of p333 and os1_15_10 on delay, close-following, flow, b3 and b45; it ties 3E-T on delay and close-following, and 3E-T is ahead on b45.
findings.numbers: 3,500 against p333 (= os1_15_10): delay −0.2 [−0.9, +0.1]; close-following −0.9 [−40.5, +29.8]; paired medians: v3w +93.8 veh·s delay, +0.2 veh·s close-following. Against 3E-T: delay +0.8 [+0.3, +1.4]; close-following −18.8 [−32.5, +39.4]; b3 −2.2 [−3.7, −0.6] (R). Against no control: close-following −272.7 [−303.6, −87.3] (medians 21.9 against 5.5 veh·s). 7,000 against p333: delay +3.7 [+2.6, +5.2], close-following +42.3 [+36.9, +45.3]; against os1_15_10: +6.6 [+1.6, +9.9], +32.6 [+22.8, +40.2]; against 3E-T: delay +4.5 [−0.7, +6.2], close-following +1.4 [−2.2, +13.5], flow +2.2 [+0.3, +2.9], b45 −29.7 [−32.6, −23.7] (R); against no control: close-following −70.4 [−76.1, −62.1], b3 −46.4, b45 −67.4 (R), delay +17.5 [+14.1, +20.6].
findings.method: As F1; seeds 7,440,900-919. Identity of p333 and os1_15_10 at 3,500 checked on every seed and every stored key; at 4,500 they differ on 3 of 20 seeds (7,440,884, 894, 895).
findings.evidence: tables.md '### B at 3,500 veh/h (S1)' and '### B at 7,000 veh/h (S1)'; results.json cells['B|3500'].identical = {os1_15_10: [p333]}.

findings.statement: Direct answer from the paired CIs. Delay and close-following together: no rule beats v3w in any of the 9 cells/levels. Delay alone: no rule beats v3w anywhere. Close-following alone: only no control (X1, B 3,500, B 7,000). Every tie on delay is with p333 or os1_15_10 (3,500-6,000), os0_10_10 (X2) or 3E-T (7,000). No fixed or tuned rule ahead of no control on close-following is also ahead of v3w on it.
findings.numbers: v3w-against-rule delay CIs: 58 in total; 44 favour v3w, 14 are ties, 0 favour a rule. Close-following: 39 favour v3w, 16 are ties, 3 favour a rule (all no control). Delay ties: X2 os0_10_10; p333 and os1_15_10 at 3,500, 4,500, 5,000, 5,250, 5,500 and 6,000; 3E-T at 7,000. Close-following ties: X2 no control; 3,500 p333/os1_15_10/3E-T; 4,500 all four; 5,000 p333/os1_15_10/3E-T; 5,250 p333/os1_15_10; 5,500 and 6,000 no control; 7,000 3E-T.
findings.method: Classification of unrounded CI bounds: A if lower > 0, R if upper < 0, = otherwise.

findings.statement: Delay/close-following front (rules only, point estimates = each controller's median over the paired seeds). v3w lies beyond the front (dominates at least one front rule, dominated by none) in X1, X2, and at 5,250, 5,500, 6,000 and 7,000, by both per-controller and paired medians. At 4,500 and 5,000 the position depends on the point method. At 3,500 v3w is inside the front, dominated by p333 = os1_15_10 by margins inside the CIs.
findings.numbers: X1 front: lr1000_16_2, 3E-X1, 3E-T, a4400_10_1 (no control is added when included); v3w dominates all four. X2 front: lr1000_10_1, 3E-X2 (+ no control); v3w dominates 3E-X2 by per-controller medians, and 3E-X2 and lr1000_10_1 by paired medians. 4,500: beyond by per-controller medians (dominates 3E-T); on by paired medians. 5,000: front is p333 alone; v3w is on by per-controller medians (p333 delay 105,944 vs v3w 111,820; close-following 327.5 vs 319.1), inside by paired medians (os1_15_10: v3w +2,594 veh·s delay, +9.8 veh·s close-following; CIs −2.4 [−5.7, +3.3] and −2.4 [−32.0, +62.4]). 5,250: beyond (dominates os1_15_10 by per-controller medians, p333 by paired). 3,500: p333/os1_15_10 delay 39,650 vs v3w 40,040; close-following 21.5 vs 21.9.
findings.method: Pareto dominance on (median all_delay, median ttc_net), both minimised; weak dominance (≤ both, < one). Cross-check repeated with medians of paired differences (rule − arm).
findings.evidence: tables.md section (3), per-cell position tables with the point-median and paired-median columns.

findings.statement: Strongest rule per cell or level (per-controller medians). Delay: lr1000_16_2 (X1), lr1000_10_1 (X2), p333 at 5,000-7,000, and p333 = os1_15_10 at 3,500 and 4,500. Close-following, excluding no control: a4400_10_1 (X1), 3E-X2 (X2), 3E-T at 3,500/4,500/5,500/6,000/7,000, p333 at 5,000, os1_15_10 at 5,250. In X2, lr1000_10_1 has a lower median delay than v3w, yet the paired effect favours v3w.
findings.numbers: X2: lr1000_10_1 median delay 226,204 vs v3w 226,353 veh·s, while the paired effect is v3w +4.1 [+0.2, +5.4]. X1: lr1000_16_2 237,184 vs v3w 230,763. Best close-following excluding no control: X1 a4400_10_1 2,216.5 vs v3w 1,808.6; X2 3E-X2 1,732.0 vs v3w 1,534.4; 7,000 3E-T 4,101.5 vs v3w 4,110.7. Best b45 rule: no control in most cells, 3E-T in X2 (389.1 vs v3w 413.2).
findings.method: Order rules by median per metric.

findings.statement: tail and sw against every rule show the same pattern as v3w. No rule is ahead of either on delay in X1, X2 or any band level. Only no control is ahead on close-following (X1 for both; B 4,500 for tail). Ties: tail with 3E-X2 on X2 delay; sw with no control and 3E-X2 on X2 close-following. On b45, 3E-T, 3E-X2, copy and, for sw in X1, a4400_10_1 are ahead.
findings.numbers: Rules ahead of tail: X1 no control (close-following, b3, b45), 3E-T (b45), copy (b45); X2 3E-T and 3E-X2 (b45); 4,500 no control (close-following, b45); 6,000 no control (b3, b45). Rules ahead of sw: X1 no control (close-following, b3, b45), 3E-T, copy, a4400_10_1 (b45); X2 no control (b3), 3E-T, 3E-X2 (b45); 6,000 no control (b3, b45), 3E-T (b45). Full CIs are in tables.md.
findings.method: As F1 with the tail arm (t0-t4) and the sw arm (s0u500-s4u500); not run in S1.
findings.evidence: tables.md section (1) tail/sw tables, section (2) band tables, section (4) table 'tail and sw, the same reading'.

findings.statement: Integrity checks done for this analysis: ttc_net = E30 + out_E30 on all 5,560 rows; every arm is complete (40 seeds in test, 20 in band and S1); 0 teleports; the band v3w-against-no-control effects reproduce round 2's stored test_result.json exactly; stored no-control medians match.
findings.numbers: 5,560 rows, 0 ttc_net mismatches. Stored X1 no-control medians: close-following 1,493.0, delay 322,813, b3 3,176.6, equal to the recomputed values. Collisions (report-only): 1 among 200 v3w learner runs in X2, 1 for lr400_13_2 in X2, 1 each for sw and baseline-v3 learners in X1, 1 for a tail learner at 5,000.
findings.method: Scripts inventory.py and precheck.py; cross-read of /home/catalin/work/phd/v5b1_runs/round2/test_result.json.

analysis.coverage_gap:
12 rules were run only in X1/X2 at 5,300 veh/h and never in band B or S1. Ten are fixed rules: os0_10_10, os1_10_0, copy, lr1000_10_1, lr1000_16_2, lr400_13_2, lr400_16_1, a4400_10_1, r4a1, z33133. Two are cell-tuned: 3E-X1 and 3E-X2 (running them under B's slowdowns tests them outside their tuning cell). Band and S1 hold only no control, p333, os1_15_10 and 3E-T.

Run counts to fill the gap (rules × levels × 20 seeds):
- the 10 fixed rules: 10 × 5 band levels × 20 = 1,000, plus 10 × 2 S1 levels × 20 = 400, total 1,400 (200 per level);
- with 3E-X1 and 3E-X2 as well: 1,200 + 480 = 1,680 (240 per level).

Also absent from S1: the tail and sw arms, 200 runs each (5 learners × 2 levels × 20). X1 and X2 themselves exist only at 5,300 veh/h. Nothing was run.
caveats: The 790 CIs are unadjusted 95 % intervals. A multiplicity adjustment widens the percentile intervals from the same bootstrap, so it can only turn A or R into ties. 'No rule ahead of v3w on delay' therefore holds under any adjustment, but the counts of v3w ahead are upper bounds.

In band and S1, 'no rule beats v3w' means only no control, p333, os1_15_10 and 3E-T. The other 12 rules, including X1's best on delay (lr1000_16_2) and X2's (lr1000_10_1) and the close-following leaders a4400_10_1 and 3E-X2, were never run at other demand levels.
With 20 seeds, band ties on close-following are low power, not equivalence. CI widths reach about 100-150 points at 5,000-5,250 (for example +45.6 [−40.8, +110.4] against p333 at 5,250).
At 3,500 and 4,500 veh/h, close-following medians are only 5.5-99 veh·s per run, so percentage effects there are large and unstable.

The front is read from point estimates. Per-controller medians and medians of paired differences disagree at 4,500, 5,000 and 5,250, and on lr1000_10_1 in X2 (lower median delay than v3w, 226,204 vs 226,353, yet the paired effect favours v3w, +4.1 [+0.2, +5.4]). Both readings are in tables.md.

Five A/R marks rest on a CI bound within ±0.05 of 0 and could flip with any resampling change: X2 v3w vs lr400_16_1 on b3; 3,500 v3w vs 3E-T on flow; 4,500 v3w vs 3E-T on delay; 5,000 v3w vs os1_15_10 on flow (R); 5,250 tail vs 3E-T on flow.
Per round 2, the 3E-X1 and 3E-X2 searches did not converge (lower bounds of their family) and 3E-T ran 40 of 100 generations. 3E-X1 failed round 2's delay filter.
Arm values are per-seed means over 5 learners; this analysis does not examine individual learners. baseline-v3 rows exist but were not compared, because they were not requested.

Rule one-liners come from the b_env.py docstrings, opponents.json and round_2_result.md. I inferred the 'no control' description (no headway commands) from the config, which has no ctrl block; I did not read the plant's default ALKS setting.
Descriptive and report-only: no pass/fail and no thesis claim. No simulations were run. Only the existing rows were read, and outputs were written only to the map_all folder.

verdicts.note: Every number matches. The arm is the per-seed mean of w0u250, w1u500, w2u250, w3u500, w4u500, confirmed from round2/val/validation.json chosen['v3w']. The sign is −1 for delay/ttc_net/b3/b45 and +1 for passed. The CI is a 2.5/97.5 percentile, default_rng(20261104), 20,000 resamples.

For example, 5,250 against p333: delay +1.3 [−8.9,+7.5], cf +45.6 [−40.8,+110.4]; 4,500 against 3E-T: delay +0.473 [+0.0316,+2.078]; 5,000 against os1_15_10: flow −0.160 [−0.179,−0.0094] R. v3w against nc reproduces round2 test_result.json['band']['v3w'] to every digit, for example 4,500 ttc −121.62 [−155.14,+7.30].

At 4,500 p333 and os1_15_10 differ on seeds 7,440,884, 894 and 895 only.

verdicts.recomputed: v3w against rules over 9 cells: delay A 44, = 14, R 0 (58); cf A 39, = 16, R 3 (all nc: X1, 3,500, 7,000); no cell has a rule R on both delay and cf. Delay ties: X2 os0_10_10; p333 and os1_15_10 at 3,500-6,000; 3E-T at 7,000.
verdicts.note: Counts and tie lists match my own classification from the unrounded bounds.

verdicts.recomputed: Fronts (rules only, per-controller medians): X1 {3E-T, 3E-X1, a4400_10_1, lr1000_16_2}; X2 {3E-X2, lr1000_10_1}; 3,500 / 4,500 {3E-T, os1_15_10, p333}; 5,000 {p333}; 5,250 {os1_15_10, p333}; 5,500 / 6,000 / 7,000 {3E-T, os1_15_10, p333}. v3w position by point and paired medians: X1 beyond/beyond; X2 beyond/beyond; 3,500 inside/inside (p333 = os1_15_10); 4,500 beyond/on; 5,000 on/inside (os1_15_10: +2,594 veh·s, +9.8 veh·s); 5,250, 5,500, 6,000 and 7,000 beyond/beyond.
verdicts.note: The numbers and positions hold under their stated definition: beyond = dominated by no rule and dominating at least one front rule. That is the weak sense. v3w dominates every front rule under both point methods only in X1. By point medians it does not dominate lr1000_10_1 in X2, p333 at 5,250 and 6,000, or 3E-T at 7,000 (4,110.7 against 4,101.5 cf). By paired medians it does not dominate os1_15_10 at 5,250 or p333 at 5,500. The answer's sentence 'v3w lies beyond the rule front in ...' leaves out this definition.
Matches. Minor point outside F7: in tables.md the X2 best-flow rule is a tie, 3E-X2 = os0_10_10 = 2,145.5, but only 3E-X2 is named.

Rules R against sw: X1 nc (cf, b3, b45), 3E-T, copy and a4400_10_1 (b45); X2 nc (b3), 3E-T and 3E-X2 (b45); 6,000 nc (b3, b45) and 3E-T (b45). No rule R on delay for either arm. Ties in X2 cf: tail against nc +1.4 [−4.4,+8.7]; sw against nc −6.7 [−12.1,+2.6] and against 3E-X2 +7.2 [−0.017,+11.7].

verdicts.recomputed: 5,560 rows, 0 mismatches of ttc_net against E30 + out_E30, 0 teleports. Collisions: 1 each for X1 s2u500, X2 w3u500, X1 d0u500, X2 lr400_13_2 and B 5,000 t0. All arms are complete (40 / 20 / 20 seeds). Stored round-2 no-control medians (X1 1,493.0 / 322,813.25 / 3,176.65) equal the recomputed ones.

verify.tables_check: I parsed tables.md and compared it with my own code (written from scratch, not importing their scripts). Effect tables: all 790 effect cells in sections (1) and (2), meaning every effect, both CI bounds and the A/=/R mark, for v3w, tail and sw against every rule at X1, X2, the five band levels and both S1 levels on all 5 metrics. Result: 0 mismatches at 0.1 rounding and 0 mark mismatches. Every cell where a rule is said to beat or tie v3w is included. Medians: all 405 cells in the section (3) median tables, with 0 mismatches. Fronts, the arm positions by point and by paired medians (v3w, tail, sw in all 9 cells) and the best-rule tables were recomputed and agree. The rule list per cell and level was verified from the rows: X1 and X2 hold 14 rules plus nc (3ex1 only in X1, 3ex2 only in X2); band and S1 hold only nc, p333, os1_15_10 and 3e; tail and sw are absent from S1. The comparison count is 2x3x15x5 + 5x3x4x5 + 2x1x4x5 = 790, but 5 of those CIs are duplicates because p333 is identical to os1_15_10 at 3,500. Robustness: none of the 790 marks changes under RNG seeds 1, 2 and 3. Every bound within 0.05 of 0 (19 of them) keeps its mark under 100 alternative RNG seeds, because the bootstrap median takes discrete values.
verify.answer_verdict: Confirmed in substance; four wording fixes are needed. (a) The braking bullet names only 3E-T and copy on b45. No control is also ahead of v3w on b45 in X1, 3,500, 4,500, 6,000 and 7,000, and on b3 in X1, X2, 6,000 and 7,000. (b) 'v3w lies beyond the rule front' uses the weak definition: dominated by no rule and dominating at least one front rule. v3w dominates the whole rule front under both point methods only in X1, and the sentence should carry the definition. (c) The caveat that the five marginal A/R marks 'could flip with any resampling change' is inaccurate. They keep their marks under 100 alternative RNG seeds. At 97.5 % intervals, 3 of the 5 become ties: 4,500 delay against 3E-T, 5,250 tail flow against 3E-T, and X2 b3 against lr400_16_1. The other 2 (3,500 flow against 3E-T, and 5,000 flow where os1_15_10 is ahead) persist even at 99 %. (d) F8's tie list leaves out tail tying no control on X2 close-following. These hold: 0 of 9 cells with a rule ahead on delay and close-following together; 0 of 58 rules ahead on delay; close-following lost only to no control (X1, 3,500, 7,000); the coverage-gap list and its counts.
missed: No control's braking lead is left out of the answer's braking bullet. It is ahead of v3w on b45 in X1 (−28.8), at 3,500 (−24.6), 4,500 (−23.8), 6,000 (−14.0) and 7,000 (−67.4). On b3 it is ahead in X1, X2, at 6,000 and 7,000. On flow, os1_15_10 is ahead at 5,000 (marginal).

v3w dominates the entire rule front by both point and paired medians only in X1. By point medians it fails against lr1000_10_1 in X2, p333 at 5,250 and 6,000, and 3E-T at 7,000. By paired medians it fails against os1_15_10 at 5,250 and p333 at 5,500. 'Beyond' in the answer is the weak sense.

The coverage-gap run counts (1,400 / 1,680) hold only if the new rule runs reuse seeds 7,440,880-919 and pair with the existing arm rows. A fresh-seed round, which CLAUDE.md requires for every new round, would also need the 4 present rules re-run (4x7x20 = 560) and v3w (5 learners x 7 levels x 20 = 700). It would need tail and sw too (700 each, band plus S1) if they are to be compared.

copy is a fixed per-road rule traced from baseline-v3's DRL policies. It counts as non-learning at run time, but its design is learning-derived. This is worth one line where it is called a non-learning controller.
Only 785 of the 790 CIs are distinct: at 3,500, p333 and os1_15_10 are the same runs, so 5 CIs repeat.

Ties that sit on a bound near 0 can turn into a rule lead only under a narrower interval, not under an adjustment. The one relevant to 'where is v3w beaten' is 4,500 b3 against 3E-T: −1.26 [−4.50, +0.041].
